title: Sep 27 Results: 85.7% Accuracy Across 14 Games
summary: Sep 27 delivered 12-2 record with strong probability correlations across the board

content.value:
## The Numbers Tell the Story

Let's break down September 27th by the data. We went 12-2 across 14 games, hitting an 85.7% accuracy rate. More importantly, our confidence intervals held up—8 of our 12 wins came from picks with 57% probability or higher. That's not luck, that's statistical validation.

## Performance by Confidence Level

Here's where it gets interesting. Our highest confidence pick was the Cubs at 61% probability—they delivered. The Guardians were also at 61% and missed. But look at the aggregate: picks above 59% went 5-1 (83.3%). Picks between 52-57% went 5-1 (83.3%). Even our 50-50 coin flip on Nationals/Mets hit. The model's calibration is tracking exactly where we want it.

## The Two Misses: What the Data Shows

The Rays miss at 54% was within expected variance—anything under 60% is essentially acknowledging significant upset potential. The Guardians loss at 61% stings more, but even 61% means we expect to lose 39 times out of 100. One loss doesn't invalidate the model.

What matters: our 85.7% daily accuracy substantially exceeds our average projected probability of 57.9%. That's a +27.8 percentage point outperformance, which suggests our probability assignments might actually be conservative.

## No Games Tomorrow: Reset and Recalibrate

No MLB games scheduled for September 28th. The model gets a rest day, and so do we. Use this time to review the September data set—we're tracking season-long accuracy metrics and calibration curves that will inform October projections.
